'''Cyril Agodi Onwumechili''' {{Audio|Ig-Cyril Agodi Onwumechili.ogg|Listen|help=no}} (20 January 1932 – 16 May 2023) was a Nigerian physicist, academic administrator, and professor of geophysics at the [[University of Ibadan]] and later [[University of Nigeria]], Nsukka. He was the fourth Vice Chancellor of the University of Ife<ref name="THISDAYLIVE 2023">{{Cite news | title=OAU Loses Former Vice Chancellor, Cyril Onwumechili at 91 |newspaper=[[This Day]]| date=2023-05-20 | url=https://www.thisdaylive.com/index.php/2023/05/20/oau-loses-former-vice-chancellor-cyril-onwumechili-at-91 | access-date=2023-06-02}}</ref> (now [[Obafemi Awolowo University]]) from January 1979 to December 1982 and the former President/Vice Chancellor of the Anambra State University of Technology, Enugu, Nigeria, from January 1983 to December 1986 (when it incubated to the now [[Enugu State University of Science and Technology]], Enugu; the now [[Nnamdi Azikiwe University]], Awka; and the now [[Ebonyi State University]], Abakaliki).<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.vanguardngr.com/2023/05/oau-mourns-fourth-vice-chancellor-professor-onwumechili/|title=OAU mourns fourth Vice Chancellor, Professor Onwumechili|date=19 May 2023|access-date=20 May 2023|location=Nigeria|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref> He delivered the Ahiajoku lecture on 20 November 2000.<ref>{{cite news|url= http://ahiajoku.igbonet.com/2000/|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20040410150130/http://ahiajoku.igbonet.com/2000/|url-status= usurped|archive-date= 10 April 2004|title= The 2000 AhỊajỌkỤ lecture:Igbo Enwe Eze: The Igbo Have No Kings|date=2000|work=Sunnews|access-date=20 May 2023|location=Nigeria}}</ref> He was the first Nigerian [[geophysicist]] and the second president of the [[Nigerian Academy of Science]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.thenationonlineng.net/2011/index.php/society/25937-celebrating-an-icon.html|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=The Nation - Celebrating an icon|access-date=7 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150709121519/http://www.thenationonlineng.net/2011/index.php/society/25937-celebrating-an-icon.html|archive-date=9 July 2015|newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]}}</ref>
He was elected as president of the academy in 1979 to succeed Professor [[Victor Adenuga Oyenuga]], the first emeritus professor of the [[University of Ibadan]] and the first African professor of Agricultural science.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Adebayo|first1=Adesoye|title=Scientific Pilgrimage: 'The Life and times of Emeritus Professor|date=25 March 2015|isbn=978-1504937856|pages=179|publisher=AuthorHouse |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OdbBBwAAQBAJ&q=Professor+Victor+Adenuga+Oyenuga&pg=PT26|access-date=7 June 2015}}</ref>

==Early life==
Onwumechili was born on 20 January 1932 at Inyi town in [[Oji River]], a city in [[Enugu State]], Eastern Nigeria.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cyril Agodi Onwumechili is a Nigerian Professor of Physics and staff of the University of Ibadan. He was the first Nigerian Nuclear physicist and the second Pre|url=https://amp.ww.en.freejournal.org/47176451/1/cyril-agodi-onwumechili.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=ww.en.freejournal.org|language=en|archive-date=20 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520151013/https://amp.ww.en.freejournal.org/47176451/1/cyril-agodi-onwumechili.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended [[King's College, Lagos]] and received a bachelor's degree in [[Physics]] from the [[University of London]] in 1953 and master's degree in physics from the University of Ibadan in 1954.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Latestnigeriannews |title=Cyril Agodi Onwumechili (1932-2023) |url=http://www.latestnigeriannews.com/p/2770599/ |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=Latest Nigerian News |language=English}}</ref> He later received a Doctorate degree from the University of London.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://thenationonlineng.net/new/nuc-rewards-17-dons-others-anniversary/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=NUC rewards 17 dons, others at anniversary|date=18 December 2013|access-date=7 June 2015|newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]}}</ref>

==Career==
Onwumechili joined the Department of physics, University of Ibadan as academic staff. He was promoted to the rank of Professor in 1962 and appointed Head of the Department of Physics and Dean of Faculty of Science at Ibadan before he left in 1966 to join the services of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka as Head of the Department of Physics.<ref name="auto"/> During the Nigerian Civil War, he was appointed Acting Vice Chancellor of the University of Science and Technology, Port Harcourt.<ref name=":0" /> After the Civil War, he took over from Associate Prof. J.C. Ene as Dean of the Faculty of Science, University of Nigeria, from December 1970 - June 1971. In 1973, he was elected the first Dean of the Faculty of Physical Sciences, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, thrice elected (1973–1974; 1975–1976; October 1978- December 1978).<ref>{{Cite web |title=History |url=https://arts.unn.edu.ng/about/history/ |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=Faculty of Arts, University Of Nigeria Nsukka |language=en-US}}</ref> Onwumechili left to become the Vice Chancellor, University of Ife (Now Obafemi Awolowo University, Ife).<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-09-03 |title=In pursuit of university excellence amid ethnic sentiments |url=https://guardian.ng/features/in-pursuit-of-university-excellence-amid-ethnic-sentiments/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2022-03-04 |newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="THISDAYLIVE 2023" />

==Death==
Onwumechili died on 16 May 2023, at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite news |title=UNIFE's First Non-Indigenous VC, Cyril Onwumechili Is Dead! |url=https://theyesng.com/unifes-first-non-indigenous-vc-cyril-onwumechili-is-dead/ |access-date=20 May 2023 |publisher=Yes! International Magazine |date=19 May 2023}}</ref>
